title: Ninth Word Fifth Point Glorification In Bowing And Prostration

questions.question: At Maghrib time, who does the person turn to?
questions.answer: He turns to Allah, the One who always lives and always remains.

questions.question: What does saying that Allah is greater than everything help a person do with worldly things?
questions.answer: It helps the person turn away from things that do not last.

questions.question: When the person stands with folded hands, what is he doing?
questions.answer: He is serving and worshipping his Lord.

questions.question: What does the person do after praising Allah?
questions.answer: He says that only Allah is worshipped and only Allah is asked for help.

questions.question: In bowing, what does the person admit about himself?
questions.answer: He admits that he is weak, needy, and small before Allah.

questions.question: In prostration, what does the person leave behind?
questions.answer: He leaves everything other than Allah.

questions.question: What does the person find when he humbles himself before Allah?
questions.answer: He finds the Most Compassionate Eternal Lord.

questions.question: What big idea about Maghrib prayer is taught in this passage?
questions.answer: It teaches that Maghrib prayer turns the heart away from temporary things and toward Allah.

questions.question: Why does the human spirit turn toward Allah at Maghrib?
questions.answer: Because the heart wants lasting beauty, and Allah alone is everlasting.

questions.question: What does the passage say Allah does with the great worlds?
questions.answer: He changes and moves them as He wills.

questions.question: What is a person showing by saying words of praise to Allah?
questions.answer: He is honoring Allah’s perfect greatness, beauty, and mercy.

questions.question: Who alone should we ask for help?
questions.answer: Allah alone.

questions.question: Why does the person bow in prayer?
questions.answer: To show humility before Allah’s power and greatness.

questions.question: What feelings are shown in prostration?
questions.answer: Love, wonder, worship, and deep humility.

questions.question: What is said about Allah when the person praises Him in sujood?
questions.answer: That Allah is far above weakness, loss, and any flaw.

questions.question: Which lasts forever in this passage: worldly things or Allah?
questions.answer: Allah lasts forever.

questions.question: At this prayer time, what kind of things does the person move away from?
questions.answer: He moves away from passing things that fade away.

questions.question: Why is Allah the right One to face in worship according to the passage?
questions.answer: Because He never dies, never changes, and always remains.

questions.question: What does the person do with his hands when he begins serving Allah?
questions.answer: He brings them together in worship.

questions.question: What two things does the person do with his words before bowing?
questions.answer: He praises Allah and asks Allah alone for help.

questions.question: What does bowing teach the person about himself and Allah?
questions.answer: It teaches that the person is weak and Allah is mighty.

questions.question: What does the person do with everything besides Allah during prostration?
questions.answer: He lets go of it and turns only to Allah.

questions.question: How does the passage describe Allah’s mercy?
questions.answer: It shows Allah as full of compassion and mercy without limit.

questions.question: What is one main lesson a student can learn from this passage?
questions.answer: We should love Allah most and worship Him with humble hearts.

questions.question: What does the spirit want by its nature in this passage?
questions.answer: It wants beauty that never ends.

questions.question: What does saying that Allah is the greatest mean about created things?
questions.answer: It means created things are not greater than Allah and should not take His place in our hearts.

questions.question: When a person says all praise belongs to Allah, what is he praising?
questions.answer: Allah’s perfect greatness, beautiful qualities, and mercy.

questions.question: What does it mean to worship Allah alone?
questions.answer: It means only Allah deserves our worship.

questions.question: What does it mean to seek help from Allah alone?
questions.answer: It means we depend on Allah above everyone and everything.

questions.question: Why does the person say he is weak and poor before Allah?
questions.answer: To show that he needs Allah and cannot stand by his own power.

questions.question: What happens in prostration to the person’s heart?
questions.answer: The heart shows love, awe, and humility to Allah.

questions.question: How does this passage help us understand Maghrib prayer?
questions.answer: It shows that Maghrib prayer is a time to remember Allah and cling to Him, not to temporary things.

questions.question: What makes Allah different from the things people may love in the world?
questions.answer: Allah never fades, never dies, and never disappears.

questions.question: What does the passage say Allah does with the huge worlds?
questions.answer: He controls them and changes them.

questions.question: What is the person doing when he rises before Allah?
questions.answer: He is standing in worship before his Lord.

questions.question: Which is correct: we worship many helpers, or we worship Allah and ask Him alone for help?
questions.answer: We worship Allah and ask Him alone for help.

questions.question: In the bowing part, what does the person say about Allah’s rank?
questions.answer: Allah is mighty, majestic, and far above the person.

questions.question: In sujood, what does the person realize about Allah’s qualities?
questions.answer: Allah’s beauty and perfection do not change or end.

questions.question: What kind of Lord does the person find when he turns fully to Allah?
questions.answer: A Lord who is eternal and full of compassion.

questions.question: What change happens in the person from the beginning to the end of the passage?
questions.answer: He turns from temporary things to full praise, worship, and humility before Allah.

questions.question: What does the person understand about the things around him at Maghrib?
questions.answer: They do not last forever.

questions.question: Why does the person face Allah instead of those passing things?
questions.answer: Because Allah alone is everlasting and worthy of worship.

questions.question: What is one way the person honors Allah while standing?
questions.answer: He praises Allah with thankful words.

questions.question: What important truth is spoken when the person says only Allah is worshipped?
questions.answer: That Allah has no partner in worship, rule, or godhood.

questions.question: What does bowing show about the person’s condition?
questions.answer: It shows that he is helpless and in need of Allah.

questions.question: What does prostration show about the person’s love for Allah?
questions.answer: It shows deep love, worship, and humility.

questions.question: According to the passage, is Allah touched by decline and faults, or is He far above them?
questions.answer: He is far above them.

questions.question: What is the best short summary of this passage?
questions.answer: Maghrib prayer teaches us to leave fleeting things and worship Allah alone with praise, need, and humility.
